item.title: North Escambia students celebrate parade book with their own balloon processions
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Students at several North Escambia elementary schools got creative after diving into "Balloons Over Broadway: The True Story of the Puppeteer of Macy's Parade" by Melissa Sweet. The book tells the history behind the iconic giant character balloons that float above New York City each Thanksgiving — and inspired the young readers to stage parades of…
item.content:encoded:
Students at several North Escambia elementary schools got creative after diving into "Balloons Over Broadway: The True Story of the Puppeteer of Macy's Parade" by Melissa Sweet. The book tells the history behind the iconic giant character balloons that float above New York City each Thanksgiving — and inspired the young readers to stage parades of their own last week, according to reporting from North Escambia.

The activity tied reading time directly to the real-world spectacle that many families tune into on Thanksgiving morning, giving kids a hands-on connection to the history behind the parade's most recognizable feature. The book itself traces the journey of Tony Sarg, the innovative puppeteer and inventor who created the first giant parade balloons in the 1920s — a creative leap that transformed Macy's annual Thanksgiving event into a national tradition.

For North Escambia students, the experience turned a holiday reading assignment into a chance to build and parade their own balloon creations, bringing the story to life in their own classrooms and schoolyards.

item.title: 650+ Volunteers Complete 43 Projects for United Way Day of Caring
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: More than 650 volunteers fanned out across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties recently to tackle community service projects as part of United Way of West Florida's 33rd Annual Day of Caring. The effort resulted in 43 completed projects at local schools and nonprofit organizations, with six of those initiatives focused on North Escambia locations.…
item.content:encoded:
More than 650 volunteers fanned out across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties recently to tackle community service projects as part of United Way of West Florida's 33rd Annual Day of Caring. The effort resulted in 43 completed projects at local schools and nonprofit organizations, with six of those initiatives focused on North Escambia locations.

The Day of Caring remains one of the largest volunteer mobilization events in the region, bringing together corporate employees, individuals, and community members to address critical needs at schools and social service agencies. Projects typically include facility improvements, mentoring programs, supply drives, and direct service work that helps strengthen local nonprofits and educational institutions.

United Way of West Florida coordinates the annual event to leverage volunteer energy and corporate resources for maximum community impact. The scope of participation—with hundreds of volunteers and dozens of simultaneous projects—underscores both the scale of local volunteer capacity and the ongoing demand for community support across the two-county area.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia is in for a mild Saturday with partly sunny skies and highs in the low 60s, but the pleasant stretch ends Sunday. Rain and gusty winds move into the area Sunday afternoon, with showers and a possible thunderstorm expected along with wind gusts reaching up to 30 mph, according to local forecasts.

If you're planning outdoor activities, Saturday offers a good window before conditions deteriorate. Those heading out Sunday should be prepared for wet, windy weather and secure any loose outdoor items.

item.content:encoded:
Dozens of people gathered Friday night at Hunter Amphitheater in Pensacola to pay respects to a family mourning the loss of their son, who died in a deadly shooting in Santa Rosa County, according to WKRG-TV 5.

The vigil brought community members together just days after the fatal incident. The gathering at the downtown Pensacola venue reflected the broader impact the loss has had on the surrounding area.

NewsRadio Pensacola is working to gather additional details about the incident and the victim. The Santa Rosa County Sheriff's Office has not yet released further public information about the circumstances of the shooting.

item.content:encoded:
Shoppers fanned out across Pensacola on Black Friday, taking advantage of holiday deals at both Cordova Mall and downtown retailers as the Christmas shopping season got underway.

According to WKRG News 5, the mix of discounts drew crowds to multiple shopping districts, with consumers eager to start their holiday gift-buying early. The downtown corridor and mall both reported activity as residents sought out seasonal bargains.

Black Friday traditionally marks the unofficial start of the Christmas shopping season, and Pensacola retailers positioned themselves to capture early-season shoppers seeking deals on gifts and holiday merchandise.

item.content:encoded:
A woman has been charged after authorities say she forced her way onto Hurlburt Field and claimed to have explosives in her vehicle, according to reporting from WKRG-TV 5. The incident raised particular concern because a child was in the car at the time, investigators said.

Details about the specific charges, the woman's identity, and the circumstances that led to the breach were not immediately available. Hurlburt Field, located in Okaloosa County near the Santa Rosa County line, is a major U.S. Air Force installation in Northwest Florida.

The incident prompted a response from base security and local law enforcement. Authorities did not immediately release information about whether any explosives were actually found or what prompted the woman's actions.

item.title: Corrections Officer Accused of Attempting to Smuggle Cell Phones Into Atmore Prison
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: ATMORE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) – An Alabama corrections officer is facing a criminal charge after state prison investigators allegedly caught her with a package of electronics intended for an inmate. The Alabama Department of Corrections says Kerry Watson was found in possession of four new cell phones, four charging cables and three pairs of…
item.content:encoded:
ATMORE, Ala. (NewsRadio 92.3) – An Alabama corrections officer is facing a criminal charge after state prison investigators allegedly caught her with a package of electronics intended for an inmate.

The Alabama Department of Corrections says Kerry Watson was found in possession of four new cell phones, four charging cables and three pairs of wireless earbuds.

Investigators determined the items were allegedly intended to be smuggled into Fountain Correctional Facility near Atmore.

Watson was arrested and booked into the Escambia County Jail in Alabama on a charge of prohibited activities.

Prison officials say unauthorized cell phones present a security risk because inmates can use them to coordinate criminal activity both inside and outside correctional facilities.

The Alabama Department of Corrections' Law Enforcement Services Division is continuing its investigation.

Officials have not announced whether any inmates will face charges in connection with the case.

item.title: Woman Arrested Following Thanksgiving Day Security Scare at Hurlburt Field
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: HURLBURT FIELD, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – A woman is facing multiple felony charges following a Thanksgiving Day security incident at Hurlburt Field in Okaloosa County. The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office says Christine Hill entered the military installation without authorization and claimed to have explosives in her vehicle. According to…
item.content:encoded:
HURLBURT FIELD, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – A woman is facing multiple felony charges following a Thanksgiving Day security incident at Hurlburt Field in Okaloosa County.

The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office says Christine Hill entered the military installation without authorization and claimed to have explosives in her vehicle.

According to investigators, Hill refused to respond to military security personnel and sheriff's deputies.

The sheriff's office deployed additional resources to assist Air Force security personnel, who eventually removed Hill from the vehicle. Deputies took her into custody without further incident.

Authorities say a child was also in the vehicle.

Hill faces multiple felony charges, including child abuse and falsely reporting the planting of a bomb.

Authorities have not publicly disclosed a motive for the incident.

item.title: Senator Moody pushes permanent support for rare pediatric disease treatments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody joined with Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on Thursday to introduce legislation aimed at ensuring long-term funding for treatments targeting rare diseases in children. The Priority for Pediatric Cures Act would make permanent the FDA's Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher Program, which has been critical in spurring…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody joined with Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on Thursday to introduce legislation aimed at ensuring long-term funding for treatments targeting rare diseases in children. The Priority for Pediatric Cures Act would make permanent the FDA's Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher Program, which has been critical in spurring pharmaceutical development for conditions that otherwise lack commercial incentive.

According to Moody's office, the program has already helped bring treatments for 47 rare pediatric diseases to market, with only four of those conditions having FDA-approved treatments before the program existed. The voucher system works by awarding transferable priority review vouchers to companies that successfully develop and gain FDA approval for qualifying treatments—a mechanism designed to offset the financial risk of investing in drugs for extremely small patient populations.

Moody emphasized the stakes for families. "For parents whose children are battling rare, life-threatening diseases, nothing is more important than having a treatment that could save their child's life," she said in a statement. Bennet noted that the program's previous lapse created uncertainty in the drug development pipeline, requiring more than a year of bipartisan effort to restore it. "Drug development takes years of commitment and innovation. This important process shouldn't be subject to stop-and-start authorization cycles in Congress," he said.

Industry groups, including the Biotechnology Innovation Organization and the Rare Disease Company Coalition, backed the measure, citing the need for predictable incentives to attract sustained investment in treatments for diseases affecting small numbers of patients.

Vinson, a Florida State University student, was the son of newly elected Escambia County Commissioner Joe Vinson. In an…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – The Pensacola community will come together this afternoon to celebrate the life of 19-year-old Carey Vinson, who was shot and killed while camping with friends in Santa Rosa County last weekend.

Vinson, a Florida State University student, was the son of newly elected Escambia County Commissioner Joe Vinson.

In an interview with WEAR Channel 3 earlier this week, the commissioner expressed gratitude for the friends who stayed with his son and attempted to save his life.

Meanwhile, Pensacola police are prepared to assist Santa Rosa County investigators. Police spokesman Mike Wood told NewsRadio on Thanksgiving morning that Chief Eric Winstrom has instructed the department to grant requests for assistance.

Today's vigil will be held from 4 to 6 p.m. at the Hunter Amphitheater at Community Maritime Park.

Funeral services are scheduled for Saturday at Harper-Morris Memorial Chapel, with visitation beginning at 9 a.m. and the service at 10 a.m.

Anyone with information about the shooting is encouraged to contact Crime Stoppers anonymously at 850-437-STOP.

item.content:encoded:
The North Pensacola Optimist Club and Florida Power & Light are teaming up to give away 150 free Christmas trees and LED light sets to Pensacola residents this Monday, November 30.

The giveaway runs from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at Hitzman Optimist Park, 3221 Langley Avenue. Trees will be available on a first-come, first-served basis, so residents looking to brighten their homes for the holidays should plan to arrive early.

According to the announcement, each household receiving a tree will also get a matching set of LED lights, making it an all-in-one package for holiday decorating. The partnership between the local Optimist Club and FPL reflects the utility's community involvement during the holiday season.

item.title: Cool Friday, Clear Saturday, Then Rain and Storms Sunday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Friday will bring mostly cloudy skies and cool temperatures across the Pensacola area, with highs reaching only near 54 degrees, according to North Escambia weather reporting. Overnight lows will dip into the mid-30s under light winds. Conditions improve Saturday as clouds gradually clear in the afternoon, allowing temperatures to rebound into the…
item.content:encoded:
Friday will bring mostly cloudy skies and cool temperatures across the Pensacola area, with highs reaching only near 54 degrees, according to North Escambia weather reporting. Overnight lows will dip into the mid-30s under light winds.

Conditions improve Saturday as clouds gradually clear in the afternoon, allowing temperatures to rebound into the low 60s. Sunday will turn noticeably warmer and breezier, with highs climbing to around 73 degrees, but rain and storm activity is expected to move into the region as well.

Residents should prepare for the transition from cool, dry weather Friday and Saturday to wetter conditions Sunday.

item.title: Walnut Hill Landfill Plans Withdrawn After Community Opposition
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A proposed 242-acre Class III landfill project in Walnut Hill has been pulled from consideration, according to Escambia County development records. The withdrawal came just before the project was set to go before the county's Development Review Committee on Wednesday, November 25. The landfill proposal had generated significant community pushback…
item.content:encoded:
A proposed 242-acre Class III landfill project in Walnut Hill has been pulled from consideration, according to Escambia County development records. The withdrawal came just before the project was set to go before the county's Development Review Committee on Wednesday, November 25.

The landfill proposal had generated significant community pushback in the Walnut Hill area. The timing of the withdrawal — immediately before the scheduled pre-application meeting — suggests the developer chose to abandon the project rather than face formal county review and continued public opposition.

Class III landfills typically accept construction debris, yard waste, and other non-hazardous solid waste. The withdrawal means the project will not move forward through the county's development approval process at this time, though no official statement has been released explaining the decision.

item.dc:creator: news6334

The parade begins at 2 p.m. Friday, November 27, with participants lining up at Government Street and Palafox Place beginning at 12:30 p.m. Costume and decorating…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – Santa Claus, the Grinch and plenty of elves will be taking over downtown Pensacola Friday as the annual Elf Parade helps usher in the Christmas season.

The parade begins at 2 p.m. Friday, November 27, with participants lining up at Government Street and Palafox Place beginning at 12:30 p.m.

Costume and decorating contests will be judged beginning at 1:25 p.m. Families are encouraged to dress in holiday costumes and decorate wagons and strollers. Participation is free.

Pensacola Winterfest activities will follow the parade, with Christmas-themed entertainment, trolley tours and opportunities for children to meet Santa and the Grinch.

Winterfest continues on select evenings through Christmas Eve. Tickets and schedules are available at pensacolawinterfest.org.

Another holiday highlight is coming December 12, when the Budweiser Clydesdales are scheduled to make their first appearance in the Pensacola Christmas Parade.

The Pensacola News Journal reports the appearance is part of the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Lewis Bear Company and Anheuser-Busch.

The Christmas parade begins at 5:30 p.m. and is expected to feature more than 100 entries, including floats, local krewes and marching bands from Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

Additional information is available at pensacolachristmasparade.org.

item.title: Pensacola Sets Monday Deadline for Remaining Hurricane Debris
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – Pensacola residents have until Monday, November 30, to get their remaining debris from Hurricane Isaias to the curb for the city's final round of storm debris collection. City officials say crews are finishing their first pass through Pensacola neighborhoods and preparing to make a second pass to collect what…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – Pensacola residents have until Monday, November 30, to get their remaining debris from Hurricane Isaias to the curb for the city's final round of storm debris collection.

City officials say crews are finishing their first pass through Pensacola neighborhoods and preparing to make a second pass to collect what remains.

As of Wednesday, crews had collected:

  • 805,671 cubic yards of vegetative debris.

  • 29,392 cubic yards of construction and demolition debris.

  • 835,063 cubic yards of debris in total.

Debris collection is suspended Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving and will resume Saturday.

Mayor D.C. Reeves emphasized that Monday's deadline does not mean every pile will be collected that day. Collection will continue into December, and pickup dates will vary by neighborhood.

Officials say most piles remaining from the first round of collection are in difficult-to-access locations, including areas near utility poles or beneath tree limbs.

Residents who believe their debris was missed during the first pass can contact the city's 311 service for assistance.

Regular yard debris collection remains suspended while hurricane debris removal continues.

Additional recovery information is available at cityofpensacola.com.

item.title: Amendment 3 Could Put Pensacola Parade Funding in Jeopardy
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – Organizers of Pensacola's Mardi Gras celebrations and other downtown parades may eventually have to shoulder more of the cost of putting on their events as the city prepares for a significant reduction in property tax revenue under Florida's Amendment 3. Mayor D.C. Reeves said Wednesday that the city is reviewing…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) – Organizers of Pensacola's Mardi Gras celebrations and other downtown parades may eventually have to shoulder more of the cost of putting on their events as the city prepares for a significant reduction in property tax revenue under Florida's Amendment 3.

Mayor D.C. Reeves said Wednesday that the city is reviewing its operations as it prepares for an estimated $7.2 million annual budget reduction.

Among the expenses being examined are the police and fire department staffing, overtime, barricades and other services the city provides for major events.

Reeves estimated those expenses can run between $40,000 and $50,000 per parade, while organizers pay an application fee of approximately $1,000. He cautioned that those figures were preliminary estimates.

The mayor said the city could explore alternatives, including changing the routes of some smaller parades to reduce staffing and equipment costs.

However, Reeves stressed that no decisions have been made and that the city has no immediate plans to withdraw support for the upcoming Christmas parade.

The city is awaiting additional guidance from state lawmakers on how Amendment 3 will be implemented. In the meantime, all 18 city departments are reviewing their spending.

Reeves also said residents will have an opportunity to weigh in on the city's spending priorities as budget discussions move forward.
